blocks.text: BRUSSELS, Belgium — The European Union and the Philippines said Tuesday that the two sides made a “breakthrough” in their talks on a long-awaited free trade deal. Brussels and the Philippines “reached substantial agreement on a Free Trade Agreement (FTA), marking a significant milestone for both sides”, EU trade chief Maros Sefcovic and Philippine trade secretary Cristina Roque said in a statement. READ: Trump bans some Canada goods as trade war swells They made the announcement after a video call, “setting the deal on a clear path towards its formal conclusion in the coming months”.
